NUCLEAR MEDICINE THYROID UPTAKE AND SCAN

DATE: 6/27/2019 9:34 AM

INDICATION: Thyroid nodule.

COMPARISON: 4/20/2019.

PROCEDURE: 
Following oral ingestion of 299.2 uCi I-123 as a capsule, images
were obtained at approximately 24 hours including pinhole images in
the anterior and anterior-oblique projections and an anterior
planar view with markers on the chin and sternal notch. The I-123
uptake in the thyroid gland was calculated based on standard probe
measurement at approximately 4 and 24 hours. 

FINDINGS: 
Anterior and oblique images show normal position of the thyroid
gland with enlargement of the lower pole of the right lobe,
corresponding to a previously seen nodule. Radiotracer uptake is
concentrated within this nodule. Minimal radiotracer uptake is
present within the background normal thyroid.

The following uptake values were obtained: 11.9% at 4 hours, 28.3%
at 24 hours. Normal ranges are 5-15% at 4 hours and 15-30% at 24
hours.

IMPRESSION:
1. Findings consistent with hyperfunctioning right thyroid nodule.
